tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description:
Withdraw a proposal you made with start_session (initiation "own_initiative" or "offer") that the user has not started.

A card the user answered has already left, "Do it here" included, so it needs no call.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Overview 6 7 The Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub is one backend service of the Project Portal (PP). It manages project assets that student teams need — software license keys and cloud credit vouchers — and gives teams a simple help desk for problems with those assets. 8 9 What it does: 10 - Instructors add assets to a shared pool 11 - Teams request assets; instructors approve or deny 12 - Approved assets are assigned to the team; the team marks them redeemed 13 - Every change to an asset or request is written to an audit log ("tracking parameters") 14 - Teams open help desk tickets about their assets; help desk staff reply, close, revoke or replace 15 16 **[Assumption]** "Logging tracking parameters" is read as: a record of which asset went to which team, when, by whom, and its status. 17 18 ## 2. Tech stack 19 20 - C# / ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) 21 - PostgreSQL 18 22 - Entity Framework Core (Npgsql provider) 23 - Docker + docker-compose (api + db containers) 24 - JSON REST API, OpenAPI/Swagger docs 25 26 ## 2a. Architecture 27 28 ### Context 29 The hub is one of four isolated Project Portal services. It runs in its own containers, owns its own database, and makes no calls to other services. Data owned elsewhere (users, courses, teams) comes from local mock files. 30 31 ### Containers 32 33 ```mermaid 34 flowchart LR 35 client["API client

# Resource Allocation & Help Desk Hub

ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) + PostgreSQL 18. See [spec.md](spec.md) for the full design.

**Current state: barebones.** Only `GET /api/v1/health` exists. It checks the PostgreSQL
connection through an EF Core `DbContext` (no tables yet).

## Layout

```
global.json                  # pins .NET SDK 10
Dockerfile                   # multi-stage: SDK build -> ASP.NET runtime
docker-compose.yml           # api (:8080) + db (PostgreSQL 18, :5432)
ResourceHub.slnx
src/ResourceHub.Api/         # Web API (Controllers/, Data/, Program.cs)
tests/ResourceHub.Tests/     # xUnit integration tests (WebApplicationFactory)
```

## Prerequisites

- .NET SDK 10 (for local build/test)
- Docker with Compose v2

## Run with Docker Compose

```bash
docker compose up --build -d
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

Expected when the database is up:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"status":"ok","database":"ok"}
```

Stop the database to see the unhealthy response:

```bash
docker compose stop db
```

```bash
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health
```

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
{"status":"unhealthy","database":"unreachable"}
```

Start it again with `docker compose start db`. Shut everything down with:

```bash
docker compose down
```

Add `-v` to also delete the database volume.

The database password defaults to `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. Override it by
setting `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in your shell or in a `.env` file next to `docker-compose.yml`
(`.env` is git-ignored). Changing it after the volume exists needs `docker compose down -v`.

## Build and run locally (without the api container)

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
dotnet run --project src/ResourceHub.Api
```

Local runs use the `Development` environment, which reads the connection string from
`src/ResourceHub.Api/appsettings.Development.json` (`localhost:5432`). The URL is printed on
start-up (default `http://localhost:5184/api/v1/health`).

## Test

```bash
dotnet test
```

Without a database, the PostgreSQL-dependent test is skipped and the rest run against an
unreachable connection string (checks the `503` path). To also run the `200` test, start the db
container and point the tests at it:

```bash
docker compose up -d db
```

```bash
RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB="Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=resourcehub_dev" dotnet test
```

## Configuration

| Setting | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ConnectionStrings:HubDb` | env `ConnectionStrings__HubDb` (compose) or `appsettings.Development.json` | Required; app fails on first DB use without it |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | shell / `.env` | Used by both containers; default `resourcehub_dev` |
| `ASPNETCORE_HTTP_PORTS` | Dockerfile | `8080` |

# Barebones API + health endpoint

## What I was asked
Build a barebones ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 10) from spec.md: `/api/v1/health` checking PostgreSQL (200/503), project layout from spec §2a, EF Core DbContext with no tables, global.json, multi-stage Dockerfile, docker-compose (api + PostgreSQL 18, api on 8080), README. Run it, call health, stop db, confirm 503. No other endpoints, entities, rules or mock data.

## What I did
- Scaffolded `ResourceHub.slnx`, `src/ResourceHub.Api` (webapi, controllers), `tests/ResourceHub.Tests` (xUnit); removed WeatherForecast samples.
- Added `HubDbContext` (empty) with Npgsql provider; `HealthController` at `api/v1/health` using `Database.CanConnectAsync` with 5 s timeout.
- Wrote 3 integration tests (WebApplicationFactory): 503 on unreachable DB, no `X-User-Id` needed, 200 on live DB (runs only when `RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB` set).
- Added global.json, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, docker-compose.yml, README.md.

- **With `docker compose up --build -d`:** both containers started. Calling `GET http://localhost:8080/api/v1/health` returned `200 {"status":"ok","database":"ok"}`.

- The project layout from spec §2a: `src/ResourceHub.Api` and `tests/ResourceHub.Tests`, in one solution file, `ResourceHub.slnx`.

- [HubDbContext.cs](src/ResourceHub.Api/Data/HubDbContext.cs) is the database connection, with no tables yet.
- [global.json](global.json), a multi-stage [Dockerfile](Dockerfile), [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) (PostgreSQL 18 with a health check; the api waits until the db is healthy) and [README.md](README.md).

- **Database password:** the default is `resourcehub_dev`, a local development value. You can override it with `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` in a `.env` file, which `.gitignore` already excludes. The connection string is only in `appsettings.Development.json` and the compose file, not in `appsettings.json`.

# DevSecOps pipeline: build + test, Docker image, Trivy, Semgrep, SonarQube Cloud.
#
# Only a broken build, a failing test or a failing Docker build fails the run.
# Scanner steps use continue-on-error and never set a failing exit code, so
# findings are reported (logs + artifacts) without blocking.

name: DevSecOps

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  DOTNET_NOLOGO: "true"
  DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT: "true"
  # Scanner images pinned by version and digest.
  TRIVY_IMAGE: aquasec/trivy:0.75.0@sha256:af6acf9a6b85dfe389a1941505c0ce9efef52a4719635e1a962f022a3d855daa
  SEMGREP_IMAGE: semgrep/semgrep:1.180.0@sha256:529ee8a277ec8adc5b534d7c74eea0a47e9de21d62852b6ba7ac6ba9566845c3
  API_IMAGE: resourcehub-api:ci

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      # Lets the health endpoint's "database reachable" test run in CI.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:18
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: resourcehub
          POSTGRES_USER: resourcehub
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ci_only_password
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U resourcehub -d resourcehub"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10

    env:
      SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
      RESOURCEHUB_TEST_DB: Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=resourcehub;Username=resourcehub;Password=ci_only_password

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # Shallow clones should be disabled for a better relevancy of analysis

      - name: Set up .NET (version from global.json)
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@a98b56852c35b8e3190ac28c8c2271da59106c68 # v6.0.0
        with:
          global-json-file: global.json

      - name: Set up JDK 21 (SonarQube scanner)
        uses: actions/setup-java@b843ebf9b913146b38da2eaa7aeddf76074ae1ad # v6.1.0
        with:
          java-version: 21
          distribution: zulu

      - name: Cache SonarQube Cloud packages
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.sonar/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar

      - name: Cache SonarQube Cloud scanner
        id: cache-sonar-scanner
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/scanner
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar-scanner
          restore-keys: ${{ runner.os }}-sonar-scanner

      - name: Install SonarQube Cloud scanner
        if: steps.cache-sonar-scanner.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner"
          dotnet tool update dotnet-sonarscanner --tool-path "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner"

      - name: Restore (locked to packages.lock.json)
        run: dotnet restore ResourceHub.slnx --locked-mode

      # ---- SonarQube Cloud wraps the one and only build ----
      # Skipped when SONAR_TOKEN is unavailable (e.g. pull requests from forks).
      - name: SonarQube begin
        if: env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" begin \
            /k:"essieanawalt_cs763-resource-hub" \
            /o:"essieanawalt" \
            /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN" \
            /d:sonar.host.url="https://sonarcloud.io" \
            /d:sonar.cs.opencover.reportsPaths="**/TestResults/**/coverage.opencover.xml" \
            /d:sonar.cs.vstest.reportsPaths="**/TestResults/*.trx"

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore

      - name: Test
        run: >-
          dotnet test ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-build
          --logger trx
          --collect "XPlat Code Coverage;Format=opencover"

      - name: SonarQube end (upload analysis)
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" end /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN"

      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: tests/**/TestResults/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload SonarQube report task
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: sonarqube-report
          # Holds the dashboard URL and task id; the full report lives on sonarcloud.io.
          path: .sonarqube/out/.sonar/report-task.txt
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # ---- Docker image ----
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build --tag "$API_IMAGE" .

      # ---- Trivy: dependencies (packages.lock.json) and image ----
      - name: Trivy dependency scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src:ro \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" fs /src \
              --scanners vuln \
              --skip-dirs '**/bin' --skip-dirs '**/obj' --skip-dirs 'reports' \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-deps.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-deps.$ext" /out/trivy-deps.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-deps.txt

      - name: Trivy image scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image "$API_IMAGE" \
              --scanners vuln \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-image.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-image.$ext" /out/trivy-image.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-image.txt

      - name: Upload Trivy reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: trivy-reports
          path: reports/trivy/
          if-no-files-found: warn

  semgrep:
    name: Semgrep (C# static analysis)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Open-source CLI with public registry rules: no Semgrep account or token.
      - name: Semgrep scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/semgrep
          docker run --rm \
            -e SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/src \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src \
            -w /src \
            "$SEMGREP_IMAGE" semgrep scan \
              --config p/csharp \
              --metrics=off \
              --sarif-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.sarif \
              --json-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.json \
              --text-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.txt

      - name: Upload Semgrep reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-reports
          path: reports/semgrep/
          if-no-files-found: warn

# DevSecOps GitHub Actions workflow

## What I was asked
Create `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` (push to main + PRs, ubuntu-latest): build + test .NET app, build Docker image, Trivy (deps + image, must detect NuGet packages, report count), Semgrep OSS CLI (no account/token), SonarQube Cloud (SONAR_TOKEN, given project/org keys, adapted from Windows/PowerShell sample to Linux/bash, sharing the main build). Scans non-blocking; only build/test failures fail. Each scanner report saved as an artifact. No commit/push. Explain how to check the run on GitHub.

## What I did
- Wrote the workflow with 2 jobs: `build` (restore, Sonar begin, Release build, test with PostgreSQL 18 service + coverage, Sonar end, docker build, Trivy fs, Trivy image, uploads) and `semgrep` (parallel).
- Turned on NuGet lock files (`Directory.Build.props`); generated `packages.lock.json` for both projects. Dockerfile now copies them and restores with `--locked-mode`.

content.text:
The workflow is in [devsecops.yml](.github/workflows/devsecops.yml). Every step except SonarQube passed when I ran it locally with the same images and flags, and actionlint reports no errors. It hasn't run on GitHub yet. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**Trivy and NuGet:** Trivy doesn't read `.csproj` files, so at first it found 0 NuGet packages. It reads lock files instead, so I turned them on in [Directory.Build.props](Directory.Build.props), which creates a `packages.lock.json` per project. With those it found:
- **Dependency scan:** 55 unique NuGet packages (8 in the API, 55 in the tests; the API's 8 are part of the tests' 55). No vulnerabilities.
- **Image scan:** the app's 8 NuGet packages, with no vulnerabilities. The Ubuntu 24.04 base image has 97 OS packages with 26 vulnerabilities (21 medium, 5 low, none high or critical). These are reported but don't fail the run.

**Semgrep:** 27 C# rules, 3 files, 0 findings. Semgrep skips the `tests/` folder by default.

**Other changes:**
- **Dockerfile:** now copies the lock files and restores with `--locked-mode`. If a package changes, run `dotnet restore` and commit the updated lock files, or the build fails.
- **[HealthController.cs](src/ResourceHub.Api/Controllers/HealthController.cs):** I changed it to a regular constructor. Semgrep's C# parser couldn't read the shorter constructor syntax and skipped part of the file.
- **Database in CI:** the workflow starts a PostgreSQL 18 container, so all 3 tests run, including the 200 health check.
- **SonarQube:** I changed the sample from PowerShell to bash. The begin and end steps wrap the one Release build and the tests, so coverage goes to SonarQube too. If `SONAR_TOKEN` isn't available, those steps are skipped. Your repo already has that secret.
- **Pinning:** actions are pinned to exact commit SHAs, and the Trivy and Semgrep images to version plus digest.

**Before the first run:** in SonarQube Cloud, go to the project's Administration → Analysis Method and turn off Automatic Analysis. If it stays on, the SonarQube step fails. The run still passes because that step doesn't block, but no results are uploaded.

**How to check the run on GitHub, after you push:**
1. Go to github.com/essieanawalt/cs763-resource-hub → **Actions** tab → **DevSecOps** workflow → click the newest run. Or run:
   ```bash
   gh run watch
   ```
2. Both jobs ("Build, test, image, Trivy, SonarQube" and "Semgrep") should show a green check. A red X means the build, a test or the Docker build failed.
3. A scanner step that hit a problem shows a warning icon but the job stays green. Click into a job and expand a step to see its output; the Trivy steps print a results table.
4. At the bottom of the run's summary page, **Artifacts** has `trivy-reports`, `semgrep-reports`, `sonarqube-report` and `test-results` (JSON, SARIF and text). To download them from the command line:
   ```bash
   gh run download
   ```
5. For SonarQube, go to sonarcloud.io → organization `essieanawalt` → project `cs763-resource-hub`. The `report-task.txt` file inside the `sonarqube-report` artifact also has the direct link.

The note is in [MyAI/PA1](../MyAI/PA1/2026-10-31_02_devsecops-workflow.md).

continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" begin \
            /k:"essieanawalt_cs763-resource-hub" \
            /o:"essieanawalt" \
            /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN" \
            /d:sonar.host.url="https://sonarcloud.io" \
            /d:sonar.cs.opencover.reportsPaths="**/TestResults/**/coverage.opencover.xml" \
            /d:sonar.cs.vstest.reportsPaths="**/TestResults/*.trx"

      - name: Build
        run: dotnet build ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-restore

      - name: Test
        run: >-
          dotnet test ResourceHub.slnx --configuration Release --no-build
          --logger trx
          --collect "XPlat Code Coverage;Format=opencover"

      - name: SonarQube end (upload analysis)
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/scanner/dotnet-sonarscanner" end /d:sonar.token="$SONAR_TOKEN"

      - name: Upload test results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: test-results
          path: tests/**/TestResults/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

      - name: Upload SonarQube report task
        if: always() && env.SONAR_TOKEN != ''
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: sonarqube-report
          # Holds the dashboard URL and task id; the full report lives on sonarcloud.io.
          path: .sonarqube/out/.sonar/report-task.txt
          if-no-files-found: warn

      # ---- Docker image ----
      - name: Build Docker image
        run: docker build --tag "$API_IMAGE" .

      # ---- Trivy: dependencies (packages.lock.json) and image ----
      - name: Trivy dependency scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src:ro \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" fs /src \
              --scanners vuln \
              --skip-dirs '**/bin' --skip-dirs '**/obj' --skip-dirs 'reports' --skip-dirs '.sonarqube' \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-deps.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-deps.$ext" /out/trivy-deps.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-deps.txt

      - name: Trivy image scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image "$API_IMAGE" \
              --scanners vuln \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-image.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-image.$ext" /out/trivy-image.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-image.txt

      - name: Upload Trivy reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: trivy-reports
          path: reports/trivy/
          if-no-files-found: warn

    name: Semgrep (C# static analysis)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

              --skip-dirs '**/bin' --skip-dirs '**/obj' --skip-dirs 'reports' --skip-dirs '.sonarqube' --skip-dirs 'evidence' \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-deps.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-deps.$ext" /out/trivy-deps.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-deps.txt

      - name: Trivy image scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/trivy
          docker run --rm \
            -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out \
            -v trivy-cache:/root/.cache \
            "$TRIVY_IMAGE" image "$API_IMAGE" \
              --scanners vuln \
              --list-all-pkgs \
              --exit-code 0 \
              --format json --output /out/trivy-image.json
          for fmt in table sarif; do
            ext=$([ "$fmt" = table ] && echo txt || echo sarif)
            docker run --rm -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/reports/trivy":/out "$TRIVY_IMAGE" \
              convert --scanners vuln --format "$fmt" --output "/out/trivy-image.$ext" /out/trivy-image.json
          done
          cat reports/trivy/trivy-image.txt

      - name: Upload Trivy reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: trivy-reports
          path: reports/trivy/
          if-no-files-found: warn

  semgrep:
    name: Semgrep (C# static analysis)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Open-source CLI with public registry rules: no Semgrep account or token.
      - name: Semgrep scan
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        run: |
          mkdir -p reports/semgrep
          docker run --rm \
            -e SEMGREP_SEND_METRICS=off \
            -e GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 -e GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=safe.directory -e GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=/src \
            -v "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE":/src \
            -w /src \
            "$SEMGREP_IMAGE" semgrep scan \
              --config p/csharp \
              --metrics=off \
              --sarif-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.sarif \
              --json-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.json \
              --text-output=reports/semgrep/semgrep.txt

      - name: Upload Semgrep reports
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: semgrep-reports
          path: reports/semgrep/
          if-no-files-found: warn

# Exclude evidence/ from scanners

## What I was asked
In `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml`, stop the scanners from reading `evidence/`: SonarQube excludes `evidence/**` and its coverage and test-result report paths only look in `tests/`; Trivy and Semgrep skip `evidence/`. Nothing else changed. No commit.

## What I did
- SonarQube begin: added `/d:sonar.exclusions="evidence/**"`; changed `sonar.cs.opencover.reportsPaths` to `tests/**/TestResults/**/coverage.opencover.xml` and `sonar.cs.vstest.reportsPaths` to `tests/**/TestResults/*.trx` (were `**/TestResults/...`).
- Trivy dependency scan: added `--skip-dirs 'evidence'`.
- Semgrep scan: added `--exclude 'evidence'`.
- Tested Trivy and Semgrep against a scratch copy of the repo with planted files in `evidence/planted/`.

## Files created / changed
- `.github/workflows/devsecops.yml` (5 lines added, 3 changed). Nothing committed.

## Decisions I made (and why)
- Trivy image scan unchanged: it scans the built image, and the Dockerfile only copies `src/`, so `evidence/` is never in the image.
- `tests/` prefix on the report paths: CI writes test output to `tests/ResourceHub.Tests/TestResults/`; old copies live under `evidence/scan-reports/test-results/...` and matched the old `**/TestResults` pattern.

## Problems / things I couldn't do
- SonarQube exclusion not tested locally (needs SONAR_TOKEN + SonarQube Cloud). Check on the next run: the SonarQube Cloud project should not list files under `evidence/`, and coverage should come only from the current run.
- My first local test loop passed the flag as one word in zsh ("unknown flag: --skip-dirs evidence"); re-ran with the flags written out. That was a test-script problem, not a workflow problem.

## Commands run / test results
- actionlint 1.7.12: OK.
- Trivy fs, planted `evidence/planted/packages.lock.json`: without skip, 3 targets including the planted one; with `--skip-dirs 'evidence'`, only the 2 real lock files.
- Semgrep `p/csharp`, planted `evidence/planted/Bad.cs` (BinaryFormatter): without exclude, 1 finding (`insecure-binaryformatter-deserialization`) in the planted file; with `--exclude 'evidence'`, 0 findings, only the 3 `src/` files scanned.
- Scratch copy deleted afterwards.
